newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen says no bid in works for Arbor.
newsitem.headline: Loewen says no bid in works for Arbor.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said Tuesday its latest acquisition of shares in Arbor Memorial Services Inc does not herald a takeover effort.

Analysts believe that both Loewen, the second biggest funeral home operator in North America, and its bigger rival, Service Corp International of Houston, are interested in acquiring Toronto-based Arbor.
"There's nothing to be read into this. It's simply as an investment," a Loewen spokesman said.
Loewen earlier said it acquired 33,600 voting and 96,000 non-voting shares of Arbor on the open market, raising its stake to 28 percent of each class from 27 percent.
In a news release, Loewen said it considers the holding to be a "strategic investment" and may increase its stake again.
Arbor's non-voting stock was down 0.75 at 24. The Loewen spokesman said the shares were acquired between 24 and 25.
Service is believed to hold about 9.8 percent of Arbor's voting shares and 29.6 percent of its non-voting shares.

Arbor is controlled by its 76-year-old chairman Daniel Scanlan. Both Loewen and Service tried but failed to gain control of Arbor in 1994. Many analysts believe that Scanlan's children would be willing to sell out when Scanlan dies.
Arbor owns 44 cemeteries across Canada and has interests in 66 funeral homes.
Service is seeking to acquire Loewen with a US$2.9 billion hostile bid.
